pageCache.pageTitle: Statement of British Values - Tatworth Primary School
pageCache.text:
Statement of British Values
As part of the Prevent Strategy at Tatworth Primary School we promote the British Values of democracy, the rule of law, individual liberty, and mutual respect and tolerance of those with different faiths and beliefs. Our activities include:
School Council: Two members of each class, are elected by their peers to represent their class as School Councillors. Selecting the councillors allows us to explore democracy in action and ensures pupils voices are heard on all aspects of school life.
Classes hold a Class Council meeting (within their classroom) then the School Councillor feeds this back to the School Council team. Each School Councillor will lead the Class Council session and record their classes’ ideas and answers to the questions posed. During 2020/21 the School Council proposals included ongoing work on the Wellbeing Oakey Dokey garden and the running track.
Eco-Warriors: Each class also have two elected Eco-Warriors.
The Eco-Warriors have worked to reduce the amount of waste and plastics brought into school and focused on the development of a bee and butterfly garden to support these species to continue to flourish in our locality.
Arts Ambassadors: Members of our school community who are interested in the arts can apply to become an Arts Ambassador. This group of children meet to promote arts across the school and go on their own art visits too! During 2022/23 they plan to support other children to enjoy the arts and continue to investigate other arts activities the school can be involved in. Next year’s project includes a large, whole-school arts project for outside.
Sports Ambassadors: There are two sports ambassadors in KS2. These children support our PE teachers and coaches to promote physical exercise and being active. They meet with children and staff to ensure our pupils’ voice is heard.
Children are also able to nominate themselves to be Librarians.
As part of children’s SMSC (Spiritual, Moral, Social and Cultural) development, we promote the British values of democracy, the rule of law, individual liberty, mutual respect, and tolerance of different faiths and beliefs.
Children will gain an understanding of these values through ongoing whole-school systems and specific lessons. For example, through: PSHE and other subject lessons, assemblies, our behaviour for learning focus, external visits and visitors, pupil voice, links within the local community, supporting and learning about local and national charities, and specifically:
Democracy:Children learn about systems of democracy within the UK during their PSHE lessons. Children also experience democracy in action during elections for children’s roles, for example our school council.
The Rule of Law:Each class discuss and agree rules and learn about our school rules. During PSHE lessons, children learn about rules and laws, and why they are necessary and important to keep everyone safe.
Individual Liberty:Children learn to appreciate their uniqueness and to understand their right to make choices during PSHE lessons and see this positively reinforced through our behaviour for learning focuses.
Mutual Respect:Children learn about the ways that people can be different and learn to celebrate and respect diversity in PSHE lessons. Through our emphasis on class discussion and group work, children experience hearing opinions that are different to their own and responding respectfully.
Tolerance of Different Faiths and Beliefs: Children learn about people’s beliefs and cultures, and how to show tolerance and respect in PSHE lessons. Through their learning in RE lessons, hearing stories from other faiths/cultures and listening to visitors, children gain an appreciation of a range of beliefs within our community and across the world.

Phonics, Reading and Maths Schemes
In Reception Class, the children learn about number through the use of Numicon apparatus.
In KS1 (Years 1 and 2) and KS2 (Years 3 – 6), we follow the White Rose Maths planning materials.
Across the school, a CPA approach is used for calculations (concrete-pictorial-abstract), where the children use a range of apparatus, then represent the apparatus using pictures, and finally represent and solve their calculation using a written method.
We place a strong emphasis on discussion during maths lessons and children are encouraged to verbally explain their thinking.
To understand how maths is taught please click on the following links.
Children in Reception, Year 1 and Year 2 receive daily phonics lessons through the Read Write Inc. scheme. We also continue to provide phonics teaching beyond Key Stage 1 for children who need further input: children will continue with phonics instruction until they can decode securely.
Phonics 1:1 tutoring will be provided for children who require extra support, for as long as they need it. We aim for all children to be able to decode securely by Year 2 so that the focus can shift to building fluency: the Read Write Inc. scheme supports this progression in children’s reading. Children will bring home a storybook that they have practised at least three times in their lessons and will also bring home decodable book bag books at just the right level for them.
Phonics is a vital aspect of children learning to read, but it is equally important that they hear a variety of texts read fluently on a regular basis. Therefore, for children in Reception and Key Stage 1 we also send home quality picture and/or chapter books for parents and carers to read to and share with their children for pleasure. Learning Behaviour Scarecrows
🌾🧑‍🌾 Our Seven Learning Behaviour Scarecrows! 🧑‍🌾🌾
Our children, with the help of parents, carers and grandparents, have been busy getting creative for a wonderful village scarecrow competition!
Organised by Tatworth Allotments Association, the competition invited us to create a scarecrow for the competition. Our School Council decided to create scarecrows around our seven Learning Behaviours. Each class designed and brought their own scarecrow to life, showcasing the fantastic creativity, enthusiasm and teamwork within our school community.
Our scarecrows were proudly displayed outside the front of school, ready for judging and for visitors to discover along the competition trail.
We are absolutely delighted that every class received a certificate in recognition of their efforts! 🏅🎉 What a fantastic achievement!
A huge well done and thank you to all our children, staff and families who contributed their time, ideas and creativity to make our scarecrows so special. We hope they have brought a smile to everyone passing by and helped spread the message about what makes a great learner!
We would also like to say a big thank you to Tatworth Parish Council and Jewson’s for their very kind donation of flint stone to fill our scarecrow buckets. Your generosity helped us bring our creations together, and we are incredibly grateful! 💚
Finally, thank you to Tatworth Allotments Association for organising such a lovely community event and giving us the opportunity to get involved.

SEND
Love of Learning and Working Together’ permeates everything that we do. We encourage all children strive to ‘Achieve and Shine’ and reach their full potential in a supportive and nurturing environment.
At different times during their school career, a child or young person may have a special educational need. The SEND Code of Practice (September 2015) defines SEND as:“A child or young person has SEND if they have a learning difficulty or disability which calls for special educational provision to be made for them. A child of compulsory school age or a young person has a learning difficulty or disability if they:• have a significantly greater difficulty in learning than the majority of others of the same age or• have a disability which prevents or hinders them from making use of educational facilities of a kind generally provided for others of the same age in mainstream schools or mainstream post-16 institutions.”
Quality first teaching underpins all educational provision. It focuses on inclusive practice and breaks down barriers to learning. For the majority of children this can be achieved by understanding the needs of individuals, identifying specific barriers and making adaptations to the environment or teaching that will enable all children to access their learning and thrive. A range of strategies may be used, such as those identified in the Somerset Graduated Response Tool. The Somerset Graduated Response Tool breaks down SEN into four broad areas of need. This targets specific support for teachers to plan and for any interventions to take place.
You can learn more about the Somerset Graduated Response here.

pageCache.text:
Behaviour for Learning
Our staff have agreed a set of Learning Behaviours for our school; these are taught and applied across the whole school, although the expectations are changed for each class as we want all our learners to succeed.
We want the children to become more independent learners by developing thinking and learning skills such as determination, curiosity, co-operation and critical thinking. We want the children to realise that their ability is not fixed or predetermined, but that it can grow and develop with effort, application and perseverance. We want to teach the children skills that will enable them to learn effectively and achieve well.
Our nine learning behaviours are: Keeping Going, Risk Taker, Respect, Motivated and Engaged, Taking Responsibility, Team Player, Aiming High, Confident Communicator and Golden Friend. Animal mascots represent each of the learning behaviours.

We regularly celebrate the achievements of our children in class, on displays, in our weekly Celebration assemblies and in our newsletters.
One they have demonstrated a learning behaviour, children in Years 1 – 6 receive a sticker depicting the animal that represents the learning behaviour.
If you are thinking of joining our lovely school, call us for an informal chat on 01460 220565 or make an appointment to visit us, and see all our fabulous learning! More information can be found on the 'Open Day' tab.

Expectations
We actively manage attendance, strongly disapproving of parents taking their children on holiday in term time. Particularly as high attendance is reflected in achievement. In 2020/21 our attendance rate was above 97%.
Any requests for holiday during term time will be forwarded for a fine if the child’s attendance is below 96% and it would result in the child missing ten or more consecutive sessions of school.
Medicines can only be kept in school and administered if they are prescribed by a doctor. All medicines must be brought to the school office and a form completed and kept with the medicine.
Children are not allowed to have medicines in their possession without the consent of the Headteacher. The medicines should be handed to and collected from the class teacher, at the beginning and end of school, or to a member of office staff.
Prescribed inhalers for asthma should be kept on the child or handed to the class teacher. They should be named.
AttendanceAttending school everyday gives your child the best chance of success.Did you know that if a child has 90% attendance they will miss 4 weeks of learning every school year? This amounts to over half of a whole academic year of lost learning across their school life!
Children with 80% attendance will miss 8 weeks of learning every school year. This is 2 years of lost learning across their school life!
Can your child afford to miss out?
Research shows that children who are not in school regularly are:
More likely to become involved in, or become a victim of crime and anti-social behaviour.More likely to fall behind due to the strong link between attendance and achieving good school results.Less Likely to achieve 5 good GCSEs (grade 9-5) compared with those with less than 8 days absences.More likely to have increased levels of anxiety due to inconsistencies and uncertainty in their routine.More likely to have low self-esteem due to finding learning increasingly hard and having missed out on key information.
What happens if your child does not attend school regularly?If your child fails to attend school regularly—even if they miss school without you knowing—the local authority may take legal action against you. Forest View will notify you if your child’s attendance level is a concern and look to work with you to put in place steps to improve it. If attendance continues to require improvement or is below 90% then the school may initiate an attendance improvement meeting (AIM).
The AIM is the start of a legal process. It is important that you engage with the school and work with the support provided to meet the agreed targets. These targets will be reviewed and progress evaluated at a review meeting. If insufficient progress is made then you may be referred to the local authority for legal intervention.
If your child’s attendance is low then you run the risk of being issued with a penalty notice or being prosecuted in court. If this happens:
Parents can be fined up to £2500 or imprisoned for failing to ensure that their child attends school regularly. Magistrates can also impose a Parenting Order, which means that the parent has to attend a counselling and guidance programme, usually a parenting class.
Illness GuidanceBeing ill may prevent your child from coming to school, but, if they can get out of bed and play or enjoy TV/video games, they should be in school.
If you do feel that your child is too ill to come to school then you should notify the school immediately and then on everyday that they will be off school for. Parents should notify the school of any absence by the start of the school day, on the day of the absence. If your child’s attendance is already poor or if they are off for a prolonged period due to illness then we may ask that you provide a doctor’s certificate to verify absences.
Leave of Absence and Holiday RequestsThe Government states that leave of absence is not permitted during term time unless there are exceptional circumstances.
Taking leave of absence without prior consent will result in unauthorised absence. The school will always refer any unauthorised leave of absence that takes place over 5 school days or more to the local authority so that a penalty notice can be issued.
Family holidays will very rarely be considered as ‘exceptional circumstances’ . The school will treat any request for leave in the same way that an employer would when considering compassionate leave. Full details of the school’s attendance procedures can be viewed in the attendance policy which can be found on our website.
Each morning all children should be dropped off, at any of the school gates, between 8.40 am and 8.50 am. After 8.50 am all gates will be locked.
We would like to stress the importance of children arriving on time as children arriving late will disturb the start of the class lesson. However, should your child be late they should report to the school office.
Please note that, for everyones safety, parents are not allowed on site without an appointment.
Parents can send non urgent messages to class teachers via homelearning@tatworthschool.co.uk. Please note that the home learning inbox will not be accessed during the school day. If a response is requested by a parent/carer, a reply will follow within 5 working school days.
For any urgent messages please email the school inbox at office@tatworthschool.co.uk or pass a message to a member of staff at the school gate. Alternatively please phone the school office on 01460 220565.

Tatworth Primary School Awarded Primary Science Quality Mark
Tatworth Primary School is proud to announce that it is one of 136 schools that hasachieved the Primary Science Quality Mark (PSQM) this month, a nationallyrecognised accreditation that celebrates a commitment to developing excellence inscience leadership, curriculum design, teaching and learning.
Led by the University of Hertfordshire, for over a decade the Primary Science QualityMark (PSQM) has been setting children on a path to a life filled with excitingpossibilities and opportunities, by giving them access to a strong foundation in qualityprimary science education. Over 7000 Quality Marks have now been awarded,impacting on the learning of almost 2,000,000 children.
PSQM is a comprehensive, evidence-informed, professional learning programmewhich equips primary science subject leaders with the knowledge, confidence, andexpert support they need to transform the quality and profile of science education intheir schools.
Helen Sizer, PSQM Director said: ‘The Primary Science Quality Mark (PSQM)recognises a school’s commitment to developing and strengthening scienceeducation, celebrating the positive impact this has on children’s learning andunderstanding of the world around them.
Our congratulations go to the whole school community on this achievement andparticularly to the school’s science subject lead Mrs Bayley, who has led this processthrough participation in the PSQM professional learning programme and by driving acycle of reflection, development and improvement across the school. Theirleadership helps to ensure that all children benefit from high-quality science teachingand learning.
Everyone involved should be very proud of the positive difference they are making tochildren’s learning and of their commitment to continuous improvement in primaryscience education.’

Admissions
Somerset Local Authority co-ordinate all applications for children who start school in Reception. These admissions arrangements should be read in conjunction with Somerset’s published co-ordinated Admissions Scheme for September 2022. They can also provide support for parents who require further help understanding the admissions process or completing application forms. All parents and carers applying for a Somerset County school place for Reception starting in September will be asked to make their application on the Council’s Local Authority Application Form.
For closing date details and further information on applying for Reception places please visit here. We strongly advise that all parents and carers take note of the closing date as late applications are processed after all on-time applications and may be disadvantaged. Applications for admission are normally considered in relation to the availability of places in the child’s chronological age group, other than in exceptional circumstances.
The Admissions Authority for Tatworth Primary School is the Governing Body.
Applications for school places in Years 1 – 6 should be made using the Somerset County Council Application Form. Parents and Carers should contact the school to arrange a school tour and/or a taster session for their child if required. Places will be allocated and administered by our Governing Body.
Parents are strongly discouraged from moving between Chard area schools. If they do this, we require parents to understand that if they have faced problems at another school, they may not necessarily disappear at Tatworth. In all cases we would expect a discussion to have taken place with the current school’s Head Teacher before requesting a move to Tatworth.

Extended School
We offer wrap-around care before and after school. All children are able to have toast during morning breakfast club and a light snack at our end of day extended provision.
Children will be met at the main gate at 7.45 am & 8.00 am.
Breakfast Club runs from 7.45am until the start of school at a cost of £4.95.
Stay and Play sessions run from the end of the school day until 4.30 pm (session 1) and 4.30 pm – 5.30 pm (session 2).
Children will be taken to the main gate at 4.00 pm, 4.30 pm, 5.00 pm.
The cost of Stay and Play is £4.75 for session 1 and £2.90 for session 2 (or part thereof). If you have registered your child for the first session but are unable to collect them until after 4.35 pm you will be charged for the second hour. Children can then be collected at 5.00 pm.
Places need to be booked in advance via ParentPay. When booking, Breakfast Club is called ‘Breakfast’ and Stay and Play session 1 ‘Afternoon’ and session 2 ‘After School’. Registers are printed at 7.45 am and 3.00 pm. If you register after these times, please also phone the Green Room mobile (see below) to check that your child is on the register.
To report absence or late registration: please call the School Office on 01460 220565, option 1.
For stay and play: on 01460 220565, option 5.
Or of you are running late to collect your child: on 01460 220565, option 2.
